note: Every question the factory may put to a System One judge, in one reviewable place. judge.py reads this file; no question text lives in Python. `stage` is where it is asked, `replaces` names the LLM judgment it stands in for when `judge.mode` is `on`, `undecided` says who gets the item when the answer is under its threshold. A noul decides true at `true_at` and false at `false_at`; a choice or score decides at `confidence`. Anything that narrows scope keeps 0.9 or stricter. State paths in backticks refer to keys of the state object the named script assembles. Answers never lift a block, pass a gate or authorise a write. Calibration rule learned on TP1-15045: a question reads its subject directly from a small state (`requirement`, `case`, `comment`, one pair of statements), never through an id looked up in a large shared state - over one shared state the judge answered `ui` with 0.9 confidence for rows whose text was not a requirement at all, because the story description beside them said so. `enabled: false` with a `calibration` note records a question that was tried and failed; judge.py never sends it. A `calibration` note on an enabled question records what it was checked against. `advisory_only: true` keeps a question a hint even when judge.mode is `on`.

judgments.replaces: nothing - reachability probe of the judge itself
judgments.instructions: Does the text say that the tests passed?

judgments.undecided: qa-scout assesses it, as without a judge

instructions.question: Would a tester of the story in `story` need the ticket in `candidate` to know what behaviour to expect or to check?
instructions.focus: Same feature or user-visible behaviour, a requirement or defect the story implements, changes, restores or depends on.

criteria.true: `candidate` defines, constrains or reports behaviour of the same feature that `story` changes, or `story` cannot be verified without it.
criteria.false: `candidate` is about a different feature, is only organisational (release, planning, access, environment request), or merely shares a product area or a person with `story`.

judgments.replaces: the reason text qa-scout writes beside a relevance decision
judgments.undecided: reason records the leaning option as unconfirmed
judgments.instructions: What is the ticket in `candidate` to the story in `story`?

criteria.defines_behaviour: States requirements, acceptance criteria or a design for behaviour the story implements or changes.
criteria.defect_in_scope: Reports a defect in the behaviour the story implements or changes.
criteria.sibling_same_feature: Another work item of the same feature; shares the feature but specifies different behaviour.
criteria.dependency: Something the story technically depends on or that blocks it, without describing the story's behaviour.
criteria.unrelated: A different feature, or organisational work with no bearing on what the story's behaviour should be.

judgments.replaces: qa-requirements-tester reading every comment to find the ones that alter scope
judgments.undecided: the comment is listed for the role to read
judgments.instructions: Does the comment in `comment` add, remove, change or clarify expected behaviour or acceptance criteria of the work described in `story`?

criteria.true: The comment states or changes what the product must do, a decision about scope, an agreed exception, or an answer to a requirements question.
criteria.false: The comment is status, scheduling, review logistics, a link with no statement, or a greeting.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, 8 comments of TP1-15045/14482/8827: scope-changing comments 0.91-0.96, logistics 0.03-0.04.

judgments.replaces: one cell of the qa-requirements-tester contradiction matrix
judgments.undecided: the pair is listed for the role as `possible`

criteria.opposite: They talk about the same thing and say opposite or incompatible things about it.
criteria.consistent: They talk about the same thing and agree.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, TP1-15045 register plus three planted conflicts (restore reverted vs not reverted; nodes draggable vs read-only; added node green vs red): planted pairs `opposite` 1.0, real pairs `opposite` <= 0.02. One pair per request; a conflict noul over a shared state did not separate them.

judgments.replaces: the first guess of the register's observable-in column; the role still cites path:line
judgments.instructions: Through which channel can an outside tester observe whether the requirement in `requirement` holds?

criteria.ui: Visible in the product's user interface: a screen, control, message, layout or navigation.
criteria.api: Visible in an API request or response: status code, payload, header, error body.
criteria.data: Visible only in stored data, a file, a log or an emitted event.
criteria.not_observable: An internal quality or intent with no outcome an outside tester can observe as stated.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, TP1-15045: 14 of 15 rows decided and matching the register; the undecided one (R-15) was the story's open owner question.

judgments.replaces: the register's ambiguity screen that produces questions to the owner
judgments.undecided: the requirement is listed for the role as `check wording`
judgments.instructions: Does the requirement in `requirement` name an outcome that a tester can check as pass or fail?

criteria.true: It names what is shown, returned, stored or refused, so a check can pass or fail.
criteria.false: The outcome is left open: it only says 'works', 'correctly', 'appropriately', 'as expected', 'user-friendly' or similar.

judgments.replaces: automation-candidacy input 1 (intent / definition of done) for a plan row
judgments.instructions: Does the story in `story` state or clearly imply that the behaviour of the requirement in `requirement` must be covered by an automated test before the story is done?
judgments.calibration: rejected 2026-09-21 on TP1-15045: 15 of 15 answers between 0.18 and 0.73, none decided. Whether a story demands automation is not stated per requirement; the input stays with qa-test-strategist.

judgments.replaces: the starting `impact` of the plan rows of one requirement (risk-policy.md: low, moderate, severe)
judgments.instructions: If the behaviour in `requirement` were silently broken in production, how bad is it for a user of this product?

criteria.signals: Looks wrong or is inconvenient; every task can still be completed and nothing false is shown or stored.
A task of this feature cannot be completed or needs a workaround; the effect is visible and reversible.
Unauthorized access, exposed or destroyed data, a false result the user may act on, or lost work.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, TP1-15045: 7 of 15 decided, 5 of those equal the strategist's impact, R-10 severe against moderate. Impact needs product context the requirement text does not carry: shown to the strategist as a hint in every mode.

judgments.replaces: the first guess of a plan row's pyramid level
judgments.instructions: What is the lowest test level at which the requirement in `requirement` can be fully verified?

criteria.unit: Pure logic of one function or class; no running service, database or browser needed.
criteria.component: One UI component or one module rendered or called in isolation with stubs.
criteria.api: A request to the running backend and its response or stored effect.
criteria.e2e: Only observable through the real user interface wired to the running backend.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, TP1-15045: every decided level (8 of 15) equals the level qa-test-strategist chose; the undecided ones split e2e against component.

judgments.replaces: qa-case-critic rubric dimension 2 (atomicity) for one case
judgments.undecided: qa-case-critic scores the dimension for this case
judgments.instructions: Does the test case in `case` verify exactly one scenario?

criteria.true: One Given-When-Then flow with one triggering action and outcomes of that one action.
criteria.false: Several independent triggering actions, several unrelated outcomes, or 'and also verify' of a different behaviour.

judgments.calibration: rejected 2026-09-21 on the 15 pinned cases of TP1-15045: 4 `fail` and 11 undecided, none passed, on cases the critic scored atomic. This factory's cases walk one scenario through several numbered When steps with one Then per step; the judge reads the steps as several scenarios. Dimension 2 stays with qa-case-critic.

judgments.replaces: qa-case-critic rubric dimension 3 (clarity) for one case
judgments.undecided: qa-case-critic scores the dimension for this case
judgments.instructions: Is every expected result (Then) of the test case in `case` a concrete outcome a tester can observe and compare, such as a named element, text, status code, field value or stored record?

criteria.true: Each Then names what is observed and the value or state expected.
criteria.false: Some Then says 'works', 'is correct', 'as expected', 'successfully', or names no observable value.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, TP1-15045: 8 of 15 pass at 0.85; the lowest scores include TC-014, where the critic found a Then saying only `4xx`. Useful as an ordering of the critic's attention; too few clean cases to shorten the review much.

judgments.replaces: qa-case-critic rubric dimension 7 (completeness against the plan) for one case-row pair
judgments.instructions: Does the test case in `case` actually check the condition described by the plan row in `plan_row`?

criteria.true: The case's When exercises the row's condition and its Then checks the row's expected outcome.
criteria.false: The case checks a different condition, only part of the row, or never asserts the row's outcome.

judgments.replaces: qa-case-critic rubric dimension 5 (negative scenarios are reachable) for one negative case
judgments.undecided: qa-case-critic scores the dimension for this case
judgments.instructions: Do the Given and When of the test case in `case` say concretely how a tester brings the product into the failing or refused situation it targets?

judgments.replaces: qa-case-critic rubric dimension 8 (seed the defect) for one case; a `true` is a design analysis, never an executed probe
judgments.undecided: qa-case-critic seeds the defect for this case
judgments.instructions: Suppose the product ignores the behaviour described in `plan_row` and does nothing, or does the old behaviour. Would at least one expected result (Then) of the test case in `case` then fail?

criteria.true: A Then compares against an outcome that only the required behaviour produces.
criteria.false: Every Then would still hold if the behaviour were missing, for example it only checks that a page opens or that no error appears.

judgments.calibration: 2026-09-21, TP1-15045: 7 of 15 pass at 0.9. A pass is a design analysis and never replaces the critic's sensitivity record for a design-review row.
